## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over AoS particles with fused mask-and-list intermediates can approach the streaming ceiling despite the 73 B/p stride.

## Layout & approach
The AoS layout at 73 B/p (68 B loop stride) offers poor locality: loop 1 touches 28 of 68 B (41% hot), loop 2 touches 4 of 68 B (5%), loop 3 touches 28 of 68 B (41%) — the rest is dead line-filler. The fused approach keeps the death verdict in registers, writing only a mask byte and list index per dead particle. The 68-byte stride exceeds the 64-byte cacheline, so every access crosses a line boundary. Working set spills L1d at N≈448 and L2 at N≈7182, placing all measured N in L3 or DRAM.

## Cache saturation
All measured points are L3-resident (10K, 100K) or DRAM (1M, 10M), past the L2 spill at 7182. At q=0.01, ns/p rises ~12% from 25.9 (L3) to 29.0 (DRAM) at the 1M transition — a modest knee from the 41% hot fraction. At q=0.5 the transition vanishes (40.3→40.9 ns/p) as respawn overhead dominates memory. The grid resolves the L3→DRAM knee at low q but washes it out at high q.

## Bandwidth
Best is 2.82 GB/s (q=0.01, N=10K) — 22% of the 12.69 GB/s ceiling, 4.5x above the 5.753 ns/p floor. Not bandwidth-bound: frontend stalls consume 62-70% of cycles, compute 30-38%, backend near zero. Vs baseline, barely faster: 1.019x at q=0.01/N=10K, 1.164x at q=0.5/N=10K. Vs the winner, 2.1-3.4x slower everywhere (3.362x at q=0.01/N=10K, 2.321x at q=0.5/N=10K), widening at low q where the winner streams efficiently.

## Assembly
No across-particle vectorization (vector-suffixed: 0). The loop processes one particle per iteration at stride 0x44 (68 B): `vmovups` loads pos+vel, `vmulps`/`vaddps` do within-particle math, `vshufps`/`vinsertps` rearrange lanes. Death uses scalar `vucomiss` + `jb`/`jae`, writing a mask byte and list index. Respawn calls `spawn` per dead particle with a PRNG chain (`rorx`, `lzcnt`). Render is a separate pass checking the mask byte (`cmp BYTE PTR [rax+r12*1],0x0` / `jne`). The 86 `mov` count and 67% frontend stalls confirm the body is too complex for fetch/decode.

## Verdict
Refuted — 0 vector-suffixed instructions means no across-particle vectorization occurred. The algo is only 1.0-1.3x faster than naive and 2.1-3.4x slower than the winner at every point. At q=0.01/N=10K: 2.82 GB/s (22% of ceiling, 4.5x above the 5.753 ns/p floor) with 67% frontend stalls; at q=0.5: 1.81 GB/s. The stride-68 AoS with 41% hot bytes, scalar `vucomiss`+branch death path, and per-particle `spawn` call make this frontend-bound — auto-vectorization cannot pack across AoS.
